title: Tenant churn mitigator and graceful retry failsafe for hosted API 5xx/timeouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: After a customer escalation last week we observed correlated 5xx waves and timeout amplification originating from tenant churn during a spike. Root cause spans a combination of proxy connection pool exhaustion, aggressive KV cache eviction during cold paths, and retry amplification triggered by non-idempotent client retries plus a fallback routing policy that fanout to multiple model variants. This ticket implements a short-term hotfix (adaptive tenant gating and idempotency enforcement) and a medium-term stabilization plan (per-tenant inflight limits, keepalive tuning, safe-fallback policy changes, and monitoring runbooks).
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant inflight request limit implemented and configurable via feature flag
Edge/proxy keepalive and connection pool settings tuned to prevent socket starvation under tenant surge
Server-side idempotency token acceptance path added for generation requests and documented SDK behavior
Fallback routing policy updated to prefer single compatible variant + controlled hedging instead of blind fanout
Automated smoke test and canary that simulates tenant churn passes in staging
Dashboards show reduction in 5xx spike amplitude and retry amplification after rollout

investigation_notes: Observed sequence: tenant surge -> many new short-lived connections -> proxy socket pool exhausted -> requests queued at edge -> KV cache cold misses spike -> longer serving latencies -> clients retry immediately -> fallback router hedges to multiple variants -> backend fanout amplifies load -> 5xx/timeouts propagate.
Proxy keepalive default (22s) caused many sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on high churn; tuning to 90s reduced churn in staging tests.

KV cache eviction policy was LRU across global tenant mix; eviction during surge evicted hot prefixes for tenants that briefly reappeared causing repeated cold paths. Need tenant-aware cache partitioning or soft-protect for recently evicted prefixes.
Client SDKs were reissuing retries without idempotency tokens; server-side idempotency gate stops duplicate work and allows safe fast-fail for already-inflight requests.

Fallback routing previously used optimistic parallel hedging to multiple variants to mask latency; under burst this converted single slow request to N slow in-flight requests. New policy will use single fallback with measured hedging if latency SLOs breached and only when capacity headroom exists.
proposed_changes: Short term (hotfix): per-tenant admission gating behind feature flag, server-side idempotency token acceptance, increase proxy keepalive and reserve connection pool slots for high-throughput frontends.

Medium term: tenant-aware KV cache partitioning and protective soft-TTL for recently evicted prefixes, per-tenant inflight quotas persisted in control-plane, and safe-fallback algorithm that avoids blind fanout.

Observability: New Grafana panels for retry amplification ratio, per-tenant inflight counts, socket pool saturation, and end-to-end idempotency collision rates. Add automated alerts tied to runbook steps.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Enable hotfix feature flag on staging and run chaos-sim tests (24h). Phase 2: Canary in prod with 10% traffic for 1 hour, check health gates (5xx rate, retry amplification, p95 latency). Phase 3: 50% for 1 hour. Phase 4: Full rollout and retrospective. Immediate rollback: disable feature flag and revert connection pool change via infra automation.

Add regression tests that simulate tenant churn and assert no amplification beyond threshold.
